page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head at the top, with page number at the top right. No margin notes. No catchword in the text; "nam" at the bottom right is the catchword.

main_text.p: nicam ab Apostolis per Spiritum sanctum mutatum fuisse, non dubito. Nam huius diei Dominicæ mentio fit in literis Apostolicis. Apoc. I. Ego Johannes fui in spiritu, in Domini-co die. Eodem autem die Dominico, id est, feria prima hebdomadis, solitos fuisse Apo-stolos, & alios Christianos convenire, Coe-nam administrare, collectas facere, & pre-cibus vacare, audireque verbum Dei, quæ antea solita erant fieri die sabbathi: liquet ex iis locis.

Act.20 v.7. Primo autem die hebdomadæ (hic est dies Dominicus) coactis discipulis ad frangendum panem (id est, ad Coenam Domini) Paulus differebat eis, &c. & protendit sermonem usque ad mediam noctem. Græcè est, ἐν τῇ μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων[?]: quæ locutio significat primam diem, phrasi Hebraica, sicut etiam Genes. 1. Et factum est mane & vespera, dies unus, id est primus. Sic Matth.28. Cùm ait μιᾶ σαββάτων[?], id est, primo die post Sabbathum: venisse mulieres ad monumentum: id quod expressit Marcus, cap.16. dicendo, Cùm autem surrexisset Iesus πρώτῃ σαββάτου[?], apparuit primum Magdalenæ. Et in quodam veteri Codice additum erat Κυριακὴ[?] Ergo primæ diei nomine Lucas significare voluit, diem quem vocamus Dominicum, quòd eo die Dominus surrexerit. page.notes: Long s normalised to s throughout. Iohannes changed to Johannes per the i/j rule. Greek words marked [?] are hard to read at this resolution; the Greek letters are the best reading of the scan. The first word, "nicam", is a fragment cut off at the left edge and is kept as printed. The paragraph break before "Apoc. I." is not marked by indent, so it is treated as a continuation. Catchword "nam" at bottom right. Page number 155 printed top right.
